dialogue:
Speaker1: Dambi's super cute and good-looking, plus he fights well and is smart.
Speaker2: Now it's the top predator. With three of them, they can take down wild boars.
Speaker1: I can't tell if you're joking, but you can't be serious, right?
Speaker2: They hunt wild boars in packs.

Speaker1: Why do they say you 'put your head up' when you go to a golf course for the first time?
Speaker2: A lot of people think it's a technical term, but it's actually a sexist expression.
Speaker1: Seems like more women use it, though?
Speaker2: It's an example of how golf got established by lower-income folks.

Speaker1: I don’t get why they keep telling depressed people to walk and exercise. It’s like telling someone with lower body paralysis that they just need to work out more to build muscle.
Speaker2: Then just say what you want. You keep complaining, so I got nothing else to say. The MZ generation knows how to speak up these days.
Speaker1: Don't judge me so easily, just empathize. I just want you to be there.
Speaker2: Do you even know how hard it is to be around someone who's depressed for a long time?
Speaker1: Then just let me live like this alone.

Speaker1: Can people in their 20s and 30s really set up a normal life while prepping for retirement?
Speaker2: I don't think so. It's really sad that people have to start their careers in debt and give up on marriage and raising kids.
Speaker1: It's really sad how they expect us to work for free, teach without pay, and pay more health insurance just because we're young.

Speaker1: If those kids are the hope for Korea, then Korea's pretty much doomed.
Speaker2: That's like a level where they can't even run a corner store.
Speaker1: At this point, they seem addicted to self-sabotage, leaving a mess everywhere they go.
Speaker2: For real, that person is the poster child for hypocrisy.

Speaker1: Is it normal for a mother-in-law to call and tell me to make seaweed soup for her son's birthday at dawn?
Speaker2: Grandmas, am I right?
Speaker1: I dragged myself out of bed, made the seaweed soup for my husband, and then got another call to check if he ate it.
Speaker2: That's some serious love for their son.
Speaker1: I told him I fed him, and then she just had to check, like, seriously drove me crazy. I almost wanted to take that seaweed soup back.

Speaker1: Golf's pricey, especially with personal training included. Even compared to gym stuff.
Speaker2: A gym trainer and a pro golfer aren’t the same, you know? It’s a whole different level from just getting a quick look at the gym.
Speaker1: You’ve never had a personal trainer, huh?
Speaker2: Comparing a pro golfer to a gym bro? That's just ridiculous.

Speaker1: Ironically, it’s tough to live in Seoul without money, but here I am, stuck in a situation where I had to come here without any.
Speaker1: Gotta live in Seoul, that's the only option.
Speaker2: The problem is that most people just use the infrastructure as an excuse to play around, while living costs in Seoul are double.
Speaker1: I guess it's because there are more jobs in Seoul, even if the pay's the same.

Speaker1: I feel like it won't be that fun even though I'm meeting up with an old classmate today.
Speaker2: Don’t bail and say you caught the flu.
Speaker1: He's a sommelier, so he can sniff out a lie like a pro. Better just go and deal with it.
Speaker2: Ain't it a waste of a precious weekend?
Speaker1: I mean, I gotta eat anyway, so I’ll just go and grab a bite.

Speaker1: I submitted my comic to a Japanese magazine, and they gave me some really thoughtful feedback.
Speaker2: That's sad, though; usually, they just trash it with a "what's this garbage?" and move on.
Speaker1: Please, master, be the master of the Korean Peninsula one more time. I’ll do better this time.
Speaker2: What the heck are those guys at Gaesensing, Sensingtun, and Sensibja even doing? No knowledge, no proper feedback, and can't even check for typos.

Speaker1: They say the older you get, the more you should open your wallet and close your mouth, right?
Speaker2: That's a timeless quote, for sure.
Speaker1: I heard the MZ generation says old folks shouldn’t open their wallets or their mouths.
Speaker2: I don't want your money or your nagging.
Speaker1: Wouldn't that be better for both of us? Honestly, even just opening my wallet feels like a lot.
Speaker2: I think the problem is talking a lot but not paying up.

Speaker1: Just drinking alone again today. What’s life anyway? Just eat what you want and enjoy it.
Speaker2: There's no friend like alcohol, for real. I don't wanna deal with backstabbers anymore.
Speaker1: Drinking alone and eating what I want without this kind of situation is the best.
Speaker2: You can get into some sketchy situations drinking alone. You might be going a bit overboard.
Speaker1: Are you my wife or something? If you keep nagging like that, you're done too.

Speaker1: I'm seriously curious what kind of life makes someone idolize gamers and get so into it.
Speaker2: It's kinda fun reading the comments from super insecure people.
Speaker1: Those League of Legends guys are just gross. I looked them up out of curiosity, and wow, they're really ugly. It's kinda funny how they draw like that.
Speaker2: Oh, he's really good-looking. The best!

Speaker1: Given the war situation, it's smart to get a drone license ahead of time. It's common sense that drone soldiers have way better survival rates than infantry.
Speaker2: I totally agree. With a drone license, you could take out enemies like it's a game, but without it, you'd just be a target, suffering and dying.
Speaker1: Just look at the Ukraine war; it’s clear. Infantry are getting wiped out by suicide drones.
Speaker2: Seems like a lot of people have drone licenses now, so if a war breaks out, becoming a drone soldier might just be a matter of luck.

Speaker1: Where'd you get that info? I live in New York and I've never seen anyone care about their socks.
Speaker2: Sounds like that YouTuber just got it wrong. They're one of those cookie-cutter shorts creators, so the info's probably bogus.
Speaker1: The U.S. isn't filled with people who have no individuality like in Korea.
Speaker2: Seems like they think everything's like Korea just 'cause they only see what they want. Gotta filter out most of those shorts for sure.

Speaker1: I'm curious what the basis is for saying there's no evidence for the defamation.
Speaker2: So why did everyone resign then? It doesn’t add up.
Speaker1: Hope they live like trash with that mindset until the coffin closes.
Speaker2: Guess you’re not embarrassed working under a president who struggles in the National Assembly. Seems like that’s your level.

Speaker1: I was totally fooled!
Speaker2: It's tough to tell them apart these days since they're so realistic.
Speaker1: I can't even tell what's real and what's fake anymore.
Speaker2: I guess thinking everything's fake is the easiest way to chill.

Speaker1: I’m spending so much on in-game stuff that I can’t even buy food or clothes, and now I’m really feeling the heat from my wife.
Speaker2: You're not any better, huh? I used to get lectured for spending too much, but now look at you.
Speaker1: I dropped 1.3 million won in just two weeks. This game is as addictive as drugs.
Speaker2: Just gotta wing it. Treat your main like an alt, and your alt like a side alt, then you won't spend much. Don’t bother with item upgrades, just do some basic self-enchanting and quit when you’re done.

Speaker1: So, obviously, we gotta follow them into the bathroom.
Speaker2: Nah, but isn’t it a bit much to watch someone pee with their pants down?
Speaker1: Isn't it kinda suspicious if they're complaining about going in together instead of just using the bathroom and getting back to the test?
Speaker2: Yeah, preventing cheating is one thing, but we gotta follow the supervision manual first. Gotta be clear on who's responsible if something goes wrong.

Speaker1: I really don’t get how the minimum wage is 13,000 won. Can you share the source?
Speaker2: It's kinda funny to complain about bread prices when you're buying coffee for 5 or 6 thousand won.
Speaker1: Minimum wage is 10,030 won. Stop being ignorant and try working at a convenience store or café. Quit rambling from your couch.
Speaker2: Wait, don’t you work? Aren’t you getting your paid leave? What’s up with that? What about severance pay? If the law’s in place, I hope it’s actually enforced.

Speaker1: It's a simple fix—just cut down on bus stops and raise fares, but they're too worried about public opinion to actually do it.
Speaker2: That's what they call mindless marketism. Is life really that simple? Are you single-celled or something?
Speaker1: It's not right to ask for subsidies when it doesn't align with the principles of supply and demand.
Speaker2: Do you not realize that all of Seoul's public transport is in the red and funded by taxes? Is that really such a simple issue?

Speaker1: If you only saved 2,000 won, that’s not saving, that’s what’s left after spending.
Speaker2: What's up with you saying that and still pushing to buy a house? You think you can swing it without a loan?
Speaker1: No way you're over 35 and still single, right?
Speaker2: If you buy, it should be in your husband’s name only, and you gotta get a notarized agreement saying there’s no property division.

Speaker1: The subway's super crowded at this time.
Speaker2: I know, right? No clue why there are so many people on Line 1 today.

Speaker1: How long do I have to listen to these idiots talking? They should just stay home and mind their business.
Speaker2: I feel like feminism's wrecking the country. Seems like second-class citizens are just talking nonsense.
Speaker1: Seriously, seeing feminism these days makes me totally lose interest in marriage. Who'd wanna be a "pompom guy"?
Speaker2: I’ve just decided to stay single. Better to live alone than get drained by a feminist, for real.

Speaker1: You could call it sales, but honestly, it’s like begging random people for a buck.
Speaker2: Begging's gotta get you something, right?
Speaker1: What kind of sales is that? It's just some lady yelling for people to come over like she's begging.
Speaker2: If even one customer shows up from that, then it counts as sales.

Speaker1: Anyway, experiencing noise between floors really makes you understand.
Speaker2: I've definitely had noise from the upstairs or next door before.
Speaker1: Noise can travel through the pillars and walls due to structural issues, so it could come from the next door or below.
Speaker2: It's really frustrating that this issue is due to the chicken coop apartment culture and shoddy construction by builders.

Speaker1: So what have we done?
Speaker2: It's shocking how much more impressive China is than we are, honestly.
Speaker1: What can we do when two giant monsters are fighting?
Speaker2: I think this deep tech wave is kinda comparable to the Sputnik shock.

Speaker1: I saw three girls with fake designer bags today, and I couldn't help but blush at how obvious it was.
Speaker2: They really think no one can tell.
Speaker1: Why go that far just to carry a designer bag?
Speaker2: They probably have their reasons, but I think rocking an eco bag is way more hip than carrying a fake.
Speaker1: I’ve never had a designer bag, but seriously, I wish they’d just leave the fakes at home.

Speaker1: Yikes, it’s a big deal if a senior singer doesn’t know a junior’s name in this hellish Korea.
Speaker2: This kind of show is so boring. Why should someone who doesn't know feel sorry? They should just work harder.
Speaker1: Just focus on making good songs, that's all that matters. Even if you pick great kids, it's tough to make it if the music's not good.
Speaker2: Not really feeling their look. Their eyes and expressions just don’t do it for me.

Speaker1: I almost quit my job when I saw how much those mukbang YouTubers are making.
Speaker2: What’s so great about watching someone slurp food like a pig and spill broth everywhere that they’re throwing money at it?
Speaker1: For real, seeing that cellulite jiggle would totally kill my appetite, but the views are crazy high.
Speaker2: I just don’t get why people watch mukbangs. No clue why they do it.

Speaker1: You know what "shopscop" means?
Speaker2: It's a Swedish term meaning 'the shame of consumption,' referring to the environmental movement on social media that encourages not engaging in unnecessary consumption that harms the environment.
Speaker1: It's a nice sentiment, but it could put a strain on small business owners instead of helping the environment.

Speaker1: I don’t get why people are freaking out about the guy wanting to light up on the balcony.
Speaker2: Don't smoke inside, whether it's the bathroom or the balcony.
Speaker1: If I wanna smoke in my own place, I guess that's my call.
Speaker2: Looks like smokers are burning more than just their cigarettes.

Speaker1: If the price is the same for human-made and robot-made stuff, do we even need to buy it?
Speaker2: Nah, why's the price the same if a robot's cooking it?
Speaker1: Still pricey and small portions, huh?
Speaker2: I tried it, and it’s just Han River ramen. Feels like you gotta really hit the robot to get it to cook right.

Speaker1: Isn't that super dangerous?
Speaker2: If you're in pain, you should go to the hospital. Going back for a massage after that is kinda weird.
Speaker1: That's why you gotta get massages from a legit acupuncturist.
Speaker2: Acupuncturists and massage therapists are on the same level, what are you even comparing?

Speaker1: Whoa, that pitcher’s got a really bad attitude. Looks like he’s trying to hit heads on purpose!
Speaker2: Love that ending where he gets payback with a hit. The bat flip was cool too.
Speaker1: We're starting to see some character issues with those players.
Speaker2: Players like that should be banned for life. It's basically attempted murder.

Speaker1: That person seems to be spreading their arms everywhere like an octopus, acting indefinitely.
Speaker2: Feels like the whole world’s getting gaslit by that guy. He’s just a frontman who talks a big game.
Speaker1: But if he talked his way into recovering rocket boosters, shouldn’t we give him some credit?
Speaker2: What’s the point? Can’t even judge a game better than a passing dog. Did his taste just vanish along with his hair?

Speaker1: It was really tough trying to leave because of my boss.
Speaker2: So that's why you were late for your plans?
Speaker1: Totally forgot to mention that. Then he just tossed some papers at me and asked me to look into it.
Speaker2: That's wild, what were you doing all day for that to happen right at quitting time?
Speaker1: I seriously think they were just trying to mess with me.

Speaker1: I’m curious where that random claim of being second in the world even came from.
Speaker2: It's probably just some random site. No clue who’s 1st, but 2nd seems legit enough.
Speaker1: In Russia, you see faces like that everywhere, so there's nothing special about it. That's probably why they're popular in East Asian countries and living in Korea.
Speaker2: Yeah, if we're talking top-tier, they'd definitely be in the U.S. or somewhere else, no reason to stick around in Korea.

Speaker1: Why am I mad when I came to work to make money?
Speaker2: Gotta know what to do before they ask. It's always the ones who can't do their job that get mad.
Speaker1: Those in charge should just keep quiet.

Speaker1: I feel like you're gonna mess up your life with that oversleeping habit. You're always late to work.
Speaker2: I’m not doing it on purpose. I hear the alarm and think just 5 more minutes, but it never works out.
Speaker1: If you’re not fixing it even though it’s about your livelihood, then something’s off with your mindset.
Speaker2: They said if I’m late one more time, I gotta quit.
Speaker1: I really think you need to get fired to wake up, tsk tsk.

Speaker1: Do guys start feeling pressure to get married in their mid-30s?
Speaker2: For sure, good women get snatched up fast.
Speaker1: Seems like a lot of people around me are getting anxious.
Speaker2: But for guys, no matter the age, having money gives an edge. Women blinded by cash are lining up.

Speaker1: It's obvious the guy's too good for her, and she's just in it for the money.
Speaker2: For real, with that face and that money, he could totally get a hot girl, but it seems like she’s got no standards.
Speaker1: Honestly, I think most guys are better off not getting married. If a woman isn’t really dependent on a guy, it’s pretty much guaranteed they’ll just end up being her slaves.
Speaker2: Sounds like she's just looking for someone to bankroll her.

Speaker1: Wouldn't it have been better to just put them on the national team and show something, even if it meant taking some heat?
Speaker2: Is it really normal to pick a player who committed school violence to represent our country? For real?
Speaker1: So should we just cancel our best lineup and then complain about getting wrecked by Japan?
Speaker2: Defending school violence is really something else. If we're gonna get wrecked anyway, what's the point of backing that up?

Speaker1: I don’t get why they brag about it like it’s something to be proud of.
Speaker2: It can all go south in an instant, even if you're wide awake. When someone’s set on scamming, you really can get caught.
Speaker1: It's all just self-inflicted, you know? Living life on autopilot leads to stuff like this.

Speaker1: Some customer said, "With no customers like this, you're gonna go under soon."
Speaker2: Sounds like they're just talking trash.
Speaker1: I’ve got a pretty tough mindset, but that really stung.
Speaker2: Let’s hit it big and seal that mouth up with cement.
Speaker1: Ugh, opened with hundreds of millions spent, and my rent and fees are ten million a month, but today’s sales are only twenty thousand.
Speaker2: Looks like the economy's really taking a hit. Too many empty shops around here.

Speaker1: If it’s not a sponsor, there’s no reason for them to meet there.
Speaker2: It's just that I'm worried about getting sued, that's all.
Speaker1: It's funny seeing a woman over forty, like Ok-soon, talking about using her body to get by while hanging out with those kinds of kids.
Speaker2: It's just packaged like they ran into each other in the U.S. or something.

Speaker1: I was in a good mood, so I binge-watched a drama all night.
Speaker2: I wanna watch too, but my sister's in the way.
Speaker1: What, did she take your iPad?
Speaker2: Yeah, so I just fell asleep while trying to watch it at night.

Speaker1: I heard there's someone who held their right arm up for 47 years for a spiritual practice.
Speaker2: Sounds like a money-making gimmick if they say it’s from religious practice.
Speaker1: Isn't it just a mental issue? I don't really get how holding up your arm relates to practice and world peace.
Speaker2: At least he won't get into a car accident with his hand up forever.

Speaker1: Do they think the contract's a joke or something?
Speaker2: For real, they should've made them study too, not just dance and sing.
Speaker1: Anyway, they're done now, so I hope they think hard about how to live moving forward.
Speaker2: South Korea's definitely not an easy place for dropouts or high school grads.

Speaker1: They say that's just the norm in Daegu.
Speaker2: Whoa, that's some serious pressure, huh? That whole 경상도 보리문디 saying makes sense now.
Speaker1: But honestly, it was only about 2 servings. Still tasted good, though.
Speaker2: At least that's a relief.
Speaker1: The joy of traveling is the good food, but when that gets ruined, it totally kills the vibe.

Speaker1: I’m excited 'cause the coin I’ve been mining is listing today.
Speaker2: Looks like there's a ton of supply. I think it’s gonna drop big time.
Speaker1: A penny's still free money, right?
Speaker2: Aren't there gotta be buyers for trades to happen? Feels like it's just sellers right now, so will it even trade?
Speaker1: As long as I’m not holding the last bomb, there’ll be some buyers at the initial listing price since it’s all just cleanup anyway.
Speaker2: What are you even hoping for when they’ve already cashed out overseas and are just listing here last?

Speaker1: Sometimes I accidentally say something in messages that makes the other person mad.
Speaker2: I used a tilde (~) once and the other person thought I was being sarcastic. Kinda complicated, right?
Speaker1: Yeah, I used "o o" and someone got mad, thinking I was ignoring them.
Speaker2: Honestly, I kinda think that too. Seems like they can't even be bothered to use vowels, right?
Speaker1: That could be true.

Speaker1: Seriously?
Speaker2: Huh? What part did they think was harassment?
Speaker1: They were all serious about it, telling me to apologize without even considering my side.
Speaker2: What’s your reasoning for saying that?
Speaker1: I was just joking around to cheer her on, had no intention of being creepy at all.
Speaker2: Looks like we can only talk about work now. Stuff like camaraderie and company spirit feels like a thing of the past.

Speaker1: Isn't that basically saying don't work if you have kids in 1st or 2nd grade?
Speaker2: Is the shortened workweek really gonna help, though?
Speaker1: I seriously wonder if they even think things through when making decisions like that.
Speaker2: Sounds like it only applies to the kids in the 늘봄 program, not all students.
Speaker1: What are single-parent families supposed to do? This feels like clueless bureaucratic nonsense.

Speaker1: It's obvious the construction company will dodge responsibility with all those day laborers on site.
Speaker2: You gotta get the personal info yourself to sue the excavator driver.
Speaker1: Construction companies are pulling all sorts of tricks to avoid paying up.
Speaker2: People are already trying this case in the court of public opinion without even reading a line of the indictment.

Speaker1: Gotta sue in cases like that. It’s just not right if you don’t. They even made a profit off it.
Speaker2: I really can’t wrap my head around making a profit off defamation. What were they thinking registering that so boldly?
Speaker1: Sounds like they barely graduated elementary school with some cash under the table.
Speaker2: I really hope they get hit hard with no leniency.
Speaker1: I really hate hate comments, but now they're finding all sorts of ways to mess with people, so I hope everyone gets punished.

Speaker1: That sounds more like a patient than a doctor. Just talks trash all the time.
Speaker2: They really elected someone like that to represent them? Acting all smart and everything…
Speaker1: So if we trash talk that person, is it considered free speech? Are we not getting sued for defamation?
Speaker2: A person like that is a pediatrician? That's gonna put kids at risk.

Speaker1: I've heard scams in secondhand trading are getting serious lately.
Speaker2: Heard you shouldn't buy used stuff, so many sketchy people out there.
Speaker1: Whoa, they’re redirecting me to links when I’m paying with my own money.
Speaker2: If you fall for that kind of stuff, you could get scammed in any deal, so best to avoid secondhand transactions altogether.

Speaker1: You think they just ran away or dodged it? Neither side's reps showed up.
Speaker2: I don’t think those gallery slackers who just click like and dislike all day would get it.
Speaker1: The article title is exaggerated; civil cases usually just have representatives show up.
Speaker2: People commenting without knowing what a legal representative is seem like they have the intelligence of a kindergartner.

Speaker1: Is it really fair to just dismiss someone as old without knowing what values or life goals they've had? I'm 92, not some aunt.
Speaker2: If you were born in '92, you're basically an aunt. Even younger soldiers call you uncle, so yeah, must be tough at 31.
Speaker1: Why are you being so narrow-minded? They could've lived through a lot, had their own struggles or love stories.
Speaker2: Why should I understand and take responsibility for a woman who's been through a lot with different guys and has a wounded body and mind?

Speaker1: A 59-year-old new hire quit after just three days.
Speaker2: If it doesn't feel right, leaving quickly is good for both sides.
Speaker1: Kinda makes me doubt the work ethic of older folks.
Speaker2: Getting older means being quick on the uptake too. Quitting fast, huh?
Speaker1: Should I be thankful they left on good terms? Guess I won't hire older folks again.

Speaker1: Stop with the nonsense, that’s just ridiculous.
Speaker2: It's not made up. It really happened in the U.S.
Speaker1: Just Google it once, it’s all there, but y’all are saying this without even checking.
Speaker2: Are you the one with reading comprehension issues?

Speaker1: Got caught trash-talking my boss anonymously on the company board, and now my info's out there.
Speaker2: I don’t even go near the bulletin board. Don’t wanna see that kind of interference.
Speaker1: I just wanted to vent, not sure why they’re making such a big deal out of it.
Speaker2: Better to avoid people with low reading comprehension.
Speaker1: I’m just trying to forget and think we’re all just sad people.
Speaker2: Think about it: a company’s for making money, not making friends.

Speaker1: I think it’s best to move out as soon as possible.
Speaker2: Gotta be careful even just to grab some chicken in this place.

Speaker1: I don’t think this divorce talk is just about this one accident; seems like there’s a lot of issues built up.
Speaker2: Isn't the fact that this incident sparked divorce talks just showing how much petty stuff has built up over time?
Speaker1: Couples are partners walking hand in hand, so when that thin thread of trust breaks, it gets tough to live together.
Speaker2: Isn't it common sense to talk things out when there are issues in a relationship? Is it normal to bottle things up and then explode all at once?

Speaker1: I'm shaking all over.
Speaker2: Again? Gotta cut off her allowance. She keeps buying them with her money.
Speaker1: I'm so disappointed; she even wrote a letter saying she'd never do it again.
Speaker2: I heard it's harder for girls to quit. They get more dependent, I guess.
Speaker1: It’s disgusting to smell smoke on my little girl, even if she is my kid.
Speaker2: You gotta be firm about this. Handle it decisively.

Speaker1: I just don’t get how people wear miniskirts in winter; they must be freezing.
Speaker2: Sounds like you don't get the basics of being stylish. In summer, you sweat it out, and in winter, you freeze your butt off to look good.
Speaker1: My mom said you can freeze to death trying to look good.
Speaker2: Long live fleece-lined tights!

Speaker1: Did you see that too?
Speaker2: For real, that’s some next-level hypocrisy.
Speaker1: It's scary to think about where and how someone learns to drive and reacts like that.
Speaker2: What can you even learn? They’ve just got issues. The only real cure is either the death penalty or just isolating themselves until they die.

Speaker1: It really hits home that parents would give their lives for their kids.
Speaker2: Kinda sad they liked it themselves.
Speaker1: Isn't raising a kid like you without abandoning them the true meaning of maternal and paternal love?
Speaker2: Still better than being abandoned like you. Shoutout to your parents for knowing you weren't human and ditching you early.

Speaker1: I’ve been hearing that small business owners are really struggling lately.
Speaker2: They say business is slow and it's tough.
Speaker1: But the funny thing is, these days it's hard to find a spot for reservations, the parking lots are full, and it's tough to get a designated driver.
Speaker2: What’s the deal? The economic indicators say the economy’s not doing well.
Speaker1: Is it just that people flock to certain places? It's all kinda weird.

Speaker1: The media says we can't live like this, but actual stats show spending's going through the roof.
Speaker2: The top 30% are doing fine, but the rest are gonna struggle.
Speaker1: Seems like the lower-level folks at companies will relate more when we talk about the top 30% with everyone traveling abroad these days.
Speaker2: Are they clueless about the overall domestic stats and income/consumption polarization?

Speaker1: I thought I'd get married quick 'cause I'm pretty and well-endowed.
Speaker2: You’ve got a personality issue that even your looks can’t cover up. You not getting that?
Speaker1: With looks like mine, rich guys should be lining up. I'm definitely marrying a wealthy dude.
Speaker2: Is there really a guy out there who can satisfy your money-loving greed?

Speaker1: I'm about to lose it over this employee who just makes excuses and talks back no matter what I say.
Speaker2: Just fire them. Why are you keeping them around?
Speaker1: I should have the power to fire them.

Speaker1: It's not being sensitive; that friend just hasn't learned anything.
Speaker2: Sounds like a tough person to work with.
Speaker1: I've dealt with a crazy woman like that before too.
Speaker2: I really can't stand people who are terrible but still get recognized for doing good work.

Speaker1: I'm so tired of my parents always fighting about money.
Speaker2: Not everyone grows up just because they get older.
Speaker1: It drives me crazy when I have to beg for a few bucks.
Speaker2: Yikes, worst parents ever. Not even helping out.
Speaker1: Can’t fix their spending habits. It’s like a bottomless pit.

Speaker1: Anyone who's been through it knows how tough it is to deal with girls, even in a simple part-time job.
